question: Why is ViT considered more flexible than a CNN backbone?
direct_answer: Because attention can learn which parts of the image should interact, rather than using a fixed local convolution pattern.
expanded_answer: A CNN hard-codes locality through convolution and pooling, which is useful but constrained. ViT can connect distant patches directly and adapt its interactions depending on the image content, making it a flexible backbone for tasks that benefit from global context and transferable features.
key_points: CNNs impose fixed local inductive bias
ViT learns token interactions from data
Global context is easier to model directly
common_wrong_ideas: ViT is always better than CNNs in every setting
Flexibility means ViT needs no training data
